title: Mai, The Psychic Girl
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fourteen-year-old Mai treats her telekinesis as a toy until the Wisdom Alliance, a secret organization seeking world control, hunts her as a weapon. Her father dies protecting her, and she goes on the run with allies, facing the agency head Kaieda and other psychic children sent against her. The 1980s series ends abruptly.
life_message: Love between parents and children, and protecting others, matters more than power.

content.note: Psychic battles with exploding heads, people thrown from high windows and gory effects (ANN column; MU Violence, Murder).
Teen hunted by assassins; father killed protecting her (publisher blurb; ANN column).
Mild fan service (skirt flips, torn shirts) and a nude bath scene of the 14-year-old lead, cut from the first US issue and restored in the book (ANN column; MU Nudity).
Grief over her father and life on the run.
Pranks with powers early on; little else.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Mai defends herself and others; no personal honor code noted.

Order vs freedom.evidence: She flees and resists an organization that wants to control her.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Her father's sacrifice and family love are central (ANN column).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Rebels against a secret elite; allies are a loose band of youths.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Psychic powers framed as science-fiction abilities, not religion.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Life on the run puts survival first.

folkways.japan: A 1980s Japanese thriller set across Japan and abroad, with the World War II past of the villain Kaieda as background.

delivery.evidence: ANN column describes an earnest, heartwarming action story without moralizing.

personified.ideology: rule of the world by a secret elite

delivery.note: The parent-child theme comes through events rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Mai and her allies survive and Kaieda is redeemed; sympathy lies with family love over elite power. The ending is abrupt (ANN column).
